subject: Inference onramp access options — per-customer isolation vs shared transport
messages:
From: Sam Wong <sam.wong@healtix.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: netops@healtix.com, eng-leads@healtix.com
Date: Mon, 25 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Healtix private deploy — connectivity constraints and ask

Hi Mina,

Quick background: Healtix is evaluating Redwood Private and will run high-sensitivity inference workloads from two on-prem DCs (primary + DR). Their security team has two absolute constraints: (1) no public egress from inference hosts (traffic must flow over private links only) and (2) zero transitive peering — they do not want their network to become routable into other customer VPCs. They also told us they have overlapping RFC1918 ranges with some cloud accounts and use Palo Alto appliances for BGP/VPN.

Can your network/architecture team sketch the practical options (VPC peering, PrivateLink/interface endpoints, site-to-site VPN with BGP) and call out operational tradeoffs given these constraints? They asked for a recommendation focused on isolation, auditability, and failover behavior.

Attaching our short requirements doc and a couple of sketches we started. Can we get a short write-up and a recommended pattern for the RFP?

Thanks — Sam
Network Operations, Healtix

[Attachment: healtix_onramp_requirements_v1.pdf]

We'll draft a short pros/cons and include an operational checklist (BGP params, MTU, HA, monitoring hooks). Expect a proposal by EOD tomorrow.

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Sam Wong <sam.wong@healtix.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Healtix private deploy — connectivity constraints and ask

Sam, Mina, team — technical rundown and quick summary of tradeoffs based on Healtix constraints: 

1) VPC Peering (direct peering between Healtix VPC and Redwood customer VPCs)
   - Pros: Low latency, no proxy hops, good for high-throughput synchronous inference calls.
   - Cons: Transitive routing is disabled by default but peering requires non-overlapping IP ranges; because Healtix has overlapping RFC1918 ranges with a few cloud accounts, peering isn't feasible for all their subnets. Peering scales poorly when we need per-customer isolation across many accounts (N^2 peering).
   - Operational notes: If peering is used, must strictly control route advertisements and use route filters. Peering also exposes a shared routing plane — not ideal for strict audit boundaries.

2) PrivateLink / Interface Endpoints (AWS-style interface endpoints that forward to ENIs in our VPCs)
   - Pros: Provides per-service, per-account network isolation — the customer connects only to our endpoint service and cannot route into other Redwood VPCs. Works despite overlapping customer IP space because traffic goes over a managed tunnel to a private IP on the interface endpoint. No transitive routing by design.
   - Cons: Slightly higher per-request latency and egress cost (endpoint charges + data processing); requires us to provision endpoint service front-ends (ENIs/NLBs) in each region and optionally per-customer if strict audit trails per account are required. Also gets more operationally complex for high-throughput workloads — need autoscaling of endpoint backends and careful socket/resource tuning to avoid connection churn.
   - Operational notes: Recommend using mutual TLS at the application layer and VPC endpoint policies. Monitor ENI counts and slow-start NLB targets for burst behavior.

3) Site-to-site VPN (IPsec with BGP)
   - Pros: Familiar to netops teams, supports overlapping IP with route filters (we can use policy-based routing or NAT on tunnel), resilient if you have dual DCs, and can be set up quickly as a temporary onramp.
   - Cons: VPNs tend to be less predictable for sustained high-throughput inference — crypto CPU, MTU/path MTU issues, and sometimes large latency variance. Also harder to do per-customer control plane separation: if we attach multiple customers to the same transit device we must strictly isolate with VRFs or separate VGWs/TGW attachments.
   - Operational notes: When using VPNs, prefer dynamic BGP sessions with proper prefix limits, keepalive timers tuned, and monitor rekey patterns. Consider hardware offload (customer firewall) for sustained throughput.

A pragmatic pattern that meets Healtix constraints (no public egress, no transitive peering, overlapping IPs):
   - Primary: PrivateLink per account for control-plane and metadata calls (model selection, health checks, control APIs) — guarantees isolation and audit logs.
   - Data-plane: Dedicated site-to-site VPN(s) from each Healtix DC to a customer-specific VGW/TGW attachment with strict route filters OR use a per-customer transit VPC with interface endpoints into that transit VPC. The aim is to avoid putting multiple customers behind a single routable plane.
   - Failover: Peer the PrivateLink control-plane to multiple AZs and keep a secondary VPN to a separate colo for emergency data-plane fallback.

I'll attach a lightweight sketch contrasting the two patterns (PrivateLink-only vs PrivateLink + VPN backup) and rough cost delta for throughput vs per-hour VPN appliances.

-David
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: candidate_topology_sketch.png]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wong <sam.wong@healtix.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Healtix private deploy — connectivity constraints and ask

Sam — short recommendation for your RFP language plus operational checklist.

Recommendation (one-paragraph): For Healtix's constraints we recommend a hybrid onramp: expose Redwood inference endpoints via per-account PrivateLink interface endpoints for control-plane and metadata activity (ensures strong isolation and auditability), and establish dedicated site-to-site IPsec VPNs (BGP) for the bulk data-plane where sustained throughput is required. The VPN attachments should be customer-specific (TGW attachments or dedicated VPN gateways) to prevent transitive routing into other customer networks. PrivateLink provides the clean isolation and audit trail; VPNs provide a familiar, high-throughput data path with predictable routing.

Operational checklist (high-level):
- BGP: agree on ASN ranges, prefix limits, and dampening policy.
- MTU: set tunnel MTU to 1400 and validate path-MTU for payloads (model artifacts + token sizes).
- NAT: avoid NAT where possible; if overlapping IPs force NAT, document NAT pools and ensure logs are retained for 180 days.
- HA: provision dual VPN tunnels from each DC to separate edge IPs; configure BFD if supported for faster failover.
- Endpoint scale: size PrivateLink backends with autoscaling groups and warm up NLB targets for burst traffic.
- Auditability: enable VPC Flow Logs for endpoint subnets and push to dedicated S3 with encryption + object lock if required.
- Security: mutual TLS for app layer, endpoint policies to restrict allowed principals, and per-customer logging streams.

I'll convert this to 1-page language for your RFP and include the bill-of-materials items (estimated ENI counts, VPN throughput tiers). Attaching a pricing worksheet and our sketch.

-Kim
Solutions Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: privatelink_vs_peering_cost_estimate.xlsx]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wong <sam.wong@healtix.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 27 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Healtix private deploy — connectivity constraints and ask

Sam — tagging next steps from Healtix POV:
1) If you can share the exact RFC1918 ranges used in each DC we will validate where peering could be viable (some smaller subnets might be peering-friendly).
2) Confirm expected sustained TPS and peak tokens/sec so we can size VPN throughput and PrivateLink backend pools.
3) If you require immutable audit retention (for compliance), let us know retention windows and we will include S3/Lock options.

We believe the hybrid PrivateLink + customer-dedicated VPN attachments meets the constraints and gives a clear operational playbook. If Healtix prefers a single-solution route we can propose PrivateLink-only with per-customer front-ends, but that carries higher per-request cost and more engineering to scale.

I'll get a written RFP blurb and simple BOM by EOD Thursday and share the draft.

-Mina
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
